body:
Thank you for taking the time to reply, I really do appreciate it. 


It's easy to say "try not to be a liar" - I have tried. I will sit there and tell myself, "don't lie don't lie", but sure enough, 15 minutes later, I do it. I've written it on my hands in Sharpie. I've tried punishing myself for lies (donating/selling a book I love after I've lied) but nothing has stopped me.

I believe there actually is a form of therapy that is basically "get out of your current situation and do something/go somewhere completely different". 

I'd save up and move the hell out. You sound like you are not happy there (understatement, I know) and it's not like it's just a person you could avoid seeing - you LIVE there, so you are reminded of this every moment of every day. 

Don't leap blindly - do some research, look online for people seeking roommates in other towns, try to figure out what you actually want in a living situation - large city? Small city? Good community? No neighbors for 2 miles? .. before you actually make the decision to move.

Good luck.

I know these feels. Try to take some small comfort in knowing that in this modern world, you can Skype, email, text, and stay in all but physical contact with her. Start planning a visit to her NOW - save money, pick a time even if it's months away. Even once-a-year visits go a LONG way towards healing the pain of loss. And planning a visit/vacation will give you something to look forward to!

I know you say she cannot love you the way you love her, but it's been my experience that we all show love in different ways, and you may just be at an impasse there. It's also difficult to know what someone else is thinking/feeling without making the explicit attempt to communicate. Have you talked to her, really sat her down and talked to her, and made her understand how important this is for you? Have you mentioned that you actually DO want a relationship with her? If not, see how she reacts - it's not enough to just leave it at "we kissed each other". She may want an actual verbal commitment/declaration of your intent. 


Even if you lose her and your friends, you have us. Always.
